newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ food prices rise in all sectors in January.
newsitem.headline: NZ food prices rise in all sectors in January.

text.p: The New Zealand Food Price Index rose 0.6 percent in January, with prices rising in all food types surveyed, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
The January increase follows a fall of 0.7 percent in December and a fall of 0.1 percent in November.
The index is now 2.4 percent higher than a year ago.

Grocery prices overall rose 0.6 percent in January, with the most significant increases in prices of potato chips, chocolate biscuits and cheddar cheese. Against the year-ago figure, grocery prices in January were 3.2 percent higher.
Prices of meat, fish and poultry rose one percent, the first increase since September 1996, with beef and sheep meat prices also recording the first monthly price rise since September.
Beef and veal prices were up 1.6 percent in January, while sheep meat prices rose four percent.
Beef prices are now 1.6 percent higher than a year ago, the first annual rise in the series since October 1993. On an annual basis, sheep meat prices were up 10.2 percent.
Overall, prices for the meat, fish and poultry sub-group were three percent higher than a year ago.

SNZ said an increase in the price of tomatoes was the main factor in an overall rise of 0.9 percent for fruit and vegetables. Falls were recorded for apples, pear and pumpkin. Overall, fruit and vegetable prices were 0.4 percent lower than in January 1996.
Restaurant meals and ready-to-eat food prices rose 0.3 percent in the month, and were up two percent on a year ago.
Prices in the North Island rose 0.7 percent, due mainly to increases in groceries, fruit and vegetables, while South Island prices rose 0.4 percent, driven mainly by rises in meat, fish and poultry.
